item.content:encoded:
Verizon’s giving away NFL Sunday Ticket for free

With the NFL preseason starting up, it’s time for football fans to lock in how they’ll be tuning into the 2026 NFL regular season. NFL Sunday Ticket, the service that streams every out-of-market Sunday game of the season, has become an essential part of any serious fan’s football-watching arsenal. However, shelling out hundreds of dollars ($480 to be exact) for a subscription isn’t quite as fun as tuning into your favorite team. Thankfully, Verizon has dropped a major deal to keep some extra cash in your wallet this season. From now until September 23, new customers who sign up for Verizon Home Internet can get NFL Sunday Ticket at no additional cost. Already locked into an internet plan? No worries. Until that same date, new and current Verizon Wireless customers can also claim free NFL Sunday Ticket by purchasing an eligible 5G phone and signing up for (or upgrading to) an Unlimited plan. Keep reading for more details on how to snag these free NFL Sunday Ticket deals today.

How to claim your free NFL Sunday Ticket subscription

There are two ways to claim a free NFL Sunday Ticket subscription from Verizon: by signing up for a new internet plan, or by purchasing a new phone and upgrading to an Unlimited plan. The terms change depending on whether you’re a new or existing Verizon customer, and there’s a bit of fine print to sift through, so let me break the deals down so you can choose which route is best for you.

Get NFL Sunday Ticket with Verizon Home Internet (new customers only)

New Verizon Home Internet customers must sign up for and maintain one of the following internet plans:

  • Verizon 5G Home Ultimate plan
  • Verizon Home Internet Lite Extra plan
  • Verizon Fios 1 Gig or higher plan

Get NFL Sunday Ticket with Verizon Wireless (new or existing customers)

  • New customers: Must purchase an eligible 5G phone and activate a new smartphone line on an Unlimited Ultimate or Unlimited Plus plan
  • Existing customers: Must purchase an eligible 5G phone and upgrade an existing line to (or activate a new smartphone line on) an Unlimited Ultimate or Unlimited Plus plan
Remember, these NFL Sunday Ticket deals expire on September 23. That feels like a ways off, but time flies—don’t let them fall off your radar before the regular season heats up.
Already a Verizon customer? Don’t worry, current customers who don’t want to purchase a new phone aren’t entirely left out in the cold. Existing Verizon Home Internet and myPlan customers can get NFL Sunday Ticket for $234, a savings of $246. This deal ends a bit sooner, though—September 2—so click the button below to get started.

item.title: New ‘Dimension 20’ Main Cast Season Revealed: Toylight
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Wondering who the cast is for the upcoming Dimension 20 season? Want to know more about ‘Dimension 20: Toylight?’ Keep reading.
item.content:encoded:
The Intrepid Heroes return as wooden toys, dollies, and stuffies

Comedy streaming service Dropout released the trailer for its new “Dimension 20” season, titled “Toylight,” this afternoon. “Dimension 20” is an anthology TTRPG actual play show featuring a new campaign setting every season, often rotating between different casts and game systems. The “Dimension 20” YouTube channel teased the release back in July with a cryptic video titled “Playtime Is Over.” The teaser juxtaposed vintage wartime footage with unsettling black-and-white toys, and we finally know why. The new season, premiering September 16 on Dropout, is about a band of toys trying to keep a dying child from losing their spark of imagination. That spark is called the Toylight, and the Intrepid Heroes must protect it from a harsh world of brightly colored warfare. Want to know more about the new “Dimension 20” season? Watch the trailer below, and read on for everything we know right now!

How to watch “Dimension 20: Toylight”

The first episode of “Dimension 20: Toylight” will premiere on Dropout on September 16. New episodes — of which there are six in total— will air weekly on Wednesday nights. 7:00 p.m. ET, to be precise. You’ll need a Dropout subscription if you want to watch the full season, but Dropout does eventually end up putting season premieres up on the Dimension 20 YouTube channel for free. However, you’ll have to wait until September 23 for the upload. I highly recommend getting a Dropout subscription. They’re not paying me to say that, I just think it’s a good value. And right now you can get 20% off your first year with the promo code FULLYEAR20.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

“Dimension 20: Toylight” cast

”Dimension 20: Toylight” is an Intrepid Heroes season, which means it uses the main cast that viewers will recognize from seasons like “Fantasy High” and “A Crown of Candy.” As always with Intrepid Heroes seasons, Brennan Lee Mulligan will DM. He will be using the 2024 version of D&D. According to the new trailer, the cast is:

  • Brian Murphy as Ol’ Clyde Horsey
  • Emily Axford as Tiddleywinks/Cutie Pie
  • Lou Wilson as Wyon
  • Zac Oyama as Avery Augustusus Archibald Tinsley
  • Siobhan Thompson as Constance
  • Ally Beardsley as Calypso

It’s unusual for the show to air two Intrepid Heroes seasons back-to-back, but Dropout is breaking the mold this year with slightly shorter seasons. “Dimension 20: City Council of Darkness,” the show’s Vampire: The Masquerade season featuring the Intrepid Heroes, just ended in July after 14 episodes. “Toylight” will only be six episodes long, bringing this year’s Intrepid Heroes episode count to 20. Intrepid Heroes seasons are usually about 20 episodes long.

The best streaming services for D&D fans

Dropout

If you’re interested at all in D&D actual play, you’ve got to check out Dropout. It’s the exclusive home for every Dimension 20 season, with every installment bigger and better than the last.

Prime Video

The other big D&D actual play show, “Critical Role,” has a working relationship with Amazon Prime. Both “Critical Role” animated series are on Prime Video, making it a must-have service for fans.

item.title: The Jonas Brothers Return to Disney With New Video Podcast Ahead of ‘Camp Rock 3’
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: After you catch the Jonas Brothers in “Camp Rock 3,” check out their video podcast “Hey Jonas!” streaming on Disney+.
item.content:encoded:
Disney+ is the best streaming service for Jonas Brothers fans

The Jonas Brothers may have long outgrown their status as teen heartthrobs, establishing themselves as a real-world, adult band, but that doesn’t mean they can’t make time for Disney Channel every now and then. The sibling trio are making a Disney comeback with the premiere of “Camp Rock 3” later this week, but that’s not the only place you’ll be able to catch them. The Jonas Brothers launched a podcast called “Hey Jonas!” back in May. Each episode, they welcome a different special guest, from Seth Meyers to Millie Bobby Brown. If you’re a fan of the brothers or are just nostalgic for their antics on “Jonas” (2009–2010, R.I.P.), this is probably a show you’ll want to hear. Or watch, since it’s a video podcast. Starting later this week, you’ll be able to watch episodes of “Hey Jonas!” through Disney+ alongside all your other favorite Jonas Brothers titles. This is due to a deal that Disney just struck with iHeartMedia to bring several actor-run podcasts to its platform. The deal also includes five other iHeartMedia video podcasts: “Pod Meets World,” “Desperately Devoted,” “Fake Doctors, Real Friends with Zach and Donald,” “StraightioLab,” and “Thanks Dad with Ego Nwodim.” So if you’re looking to follow your favorite actors but haven’t been able to get into podcasts before, this could be a great starting point. Since they’re video podcasts, they feel much more like traditional shows. Want to learn more about “Hey Jonas!”? Keep reading to learn everything we know so far.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

How to watch “Hey Jonas!”

”Hey Jonas!” is already available in all of the usual podcast places, including Apple Podcasts and YouTube. But since it’s a video podcast, you might want to watch it along with the rest of your favorite shows. And that’s where Disney+ comes in. Thanks to this new deal between Disney and iHeartMedia, you’ll be able to watch episodes of “Hey Jonas!” on Disney+ starting August 14. If that date sounds familiar, it’s because that’s also the day that “Camp Rock 3” is premiering on Disney+. (It’s actually premiering the day before on the Disney Channel, but Disney Channel titles always come to Disney+ the next day.) It’s not currently clear whether Disney+ will also host the bonus features and other exclusives usually only found on the iHeartRadio app.

Disney+

Disney+ has all of the Disney channel classics you remember from your childhood, plus reboots of franchises like “Wizards of Waverly Place” and, of course, “Camp Rock.”

item.title: Disney+ Will Simulcast More College Football as Disney Bets on Sports to Drive Bundle Upgrades
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Disney+ will add more college football simulcasts this fall as it expands live sports coverage and promotes its ESPN Unlimited streaming bundle.
item.content:encoded:
More college football is coming to Disney+ this fall

Disney+ subscribers who also love, or even just dabble in, watching live sports will have more content available this fall, just in time for college football season. Disney held an earnings call on Wednesday, August 5. In advance of that, the company released a Q3 shareholder letter that touted higher revenues and outlined its strategy in the near future. Part of that strategy is more live sports. “We plan to deliver a more robust subset of games for Disney+ subscribers beginning this fall, anchored by additional college football simulcasts,” the company wrote in the letter. Disney+ already offers select simulcasts, alt casts, and streaming exclusives for the NBA, WNBA, NWSL, and major tennis tournaments. One of its featured simulcasts is “College GameDay.” The uptick in live sports marks not just a change in what Disney+ subscribers can expect moving forward, but also where Disney as a company hopes to lead consumers.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Disney wants live sports to drive streaming bundle upgrades

Executives seemed quite candid when discussing their live sports strategy during the earnings call. “Live sports aren’t just a viewership play, they’re a fan engagement and ecosystem play,” Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro said on the call. CFO Hugh Johnston went into more detail. “Our strategy on Disney+ is to bring additional sports content to Disney+ users and to drive additional upsell into Disney+, Hulu, and the ESPN Unlimited bundle,” Johnston said. “You can expect us to lean in in all of these areas.”

CableTV.com verdict: Disney continues pushing the envelope in sports streaming

Disney openly saying it will add even more live sports to Disney+ in order to lead fans to its bundle is a logical business step. It’s also a situation that caters to fans who value their wallets. For decades, the best and most reliable way to watch live sports was through a cable or satellite TV provider. Those plans came with expensive, years-long contracts, but we didn’t have much of a choice. The advent of streaming caused many to find their entertainment elsewhere, often for less money and more convenience. But sports lagged behind for a while. Now, seemingly every company is either getting into live sports or expanding on it. Disney+ launched its live sports initiative in late 2024, and has built upon it ever since. Then, the service’s parent company introduced ESPN Unlimited, a streaming plan specifically for sports-loving cord-cutters. Those who watch sports year-round don’t need much more than ESPN’s family of networks, to be honest, especially with its new agreement with The CW. The bundle that includes Hulu + Live TV gets fans access to other local stations like CBS, FOX, and NBC. And if Disney finds a way to incorporate regional sports network access directly to ESPN Unlimited or Disney+? That might be game over for the competition.

item.title: Broadcast Monopolies Just Became More Powerful, Thanks to Controversial FCC Vote
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Brendan Carr’s FCC just voted to repeal a 22-year-old restriction on broadcast monopolies. Read on for more info.
item.content:encoded:
FCC removes broadcast cap: Will increasing scale do any good?

Up until now, broadcast companies were not allowed to reach any more than 39% of American viewers with their portfolios of local stations. So while your local news channel might be owned by Sinclair, another might be owned by Nexstar. But the FCC just repealed that rule, which had been on the books for 22 years. The FCC’s chairman, Brendan Carr, has been a vocal opponent to the rule for a while. In the Breitbart op-ed he wrote last month, he rallies against “the values of New York and Hollywood executives,” a stance he’s also made quite clear in his time as chairman. Remember when Jimmy Kimmel got chased off the air? That was Brendan Carr’s work. But with Kimmel restored to the airwaves, Carr found himself a different target: the broadcast cap. Since streaming services are allowed to reach 100% of the country, he argues, why shouldn’t local channel providers? If more local stations could join forces, (lumped under corporate umbrellas), they would have the “power to preempt or refuse to air national programming that does not fit their communities’ values.” It seems impossible to separate this viewpoint from the Kimmel scandal, where Carr tried to remove programming that went against his own values. But I’m getting ahead of myself. I know anything to do with the FCC and airwave regulations is going to be a bit confusing, but I’ll do my best to explain.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Can they do that?

Technically, the FCC has already been allowing companies to skirt the ownership cap. Nexstar recently merged with Tegna, giving it a direct connection to 80% of the country. According to the letter of the law, that shouldn’t have happened. But the FCC gave it a pass ahead of the vote to repeal the ban. And now that the repeal has gone through, other companies might follow suit. Or Nexstar could continue merging with more companies. Let’s go into why that may be a problem.

What’s the immediate impact?

Once again, this is a bit of a free speech issue. While a private company like Disney would be free to censor a comedian however they choose, a government-backed regulatory agency like the FCC cannot. So if Carr is trying to aid companies in silencing certain viewpoints and programs, that gets into some sketchy territory. And then there’s the big issue, the one that made you click on this article: monopolies. Talking about giving the little guy more power is all well and good, but that’s not really what this repeal is going to end up doing. Local channels aren’t usually standalone operations. They’re usually owned by a larger corporation, like Sinclair or Nexstar. So what this repeal will really do is give those corporations the power to buy more networks, expanding their monopoly over the airwaves. And as we’ve seen with the equally controversial Paramount/Warner Bros. merger, monopolies spell bad news for consumers. They give companies the freedom to raise prices without competition. But broadcast corporations have been envious of that merger, and until now this cap has prevented them from operating with the unregulated abandon of streaming services. And instead of regulating those streaming services, the FCC’s solution was to level the playing field by removing the existing regulations on broadcast TV. When it comes to American media, monopolies could have disastrous political consequences. Imagine if every news channel was forced to conform to just one viewpoint—the viewpoint of whichever media conglomerate CEO owned the most airwave real estate. It would make distinguishing fact from fiction a whole lot harder. We’re already seeing those dangers in cases like the Paramount merger, which would give CEO David Ellison the same control over news network CNN that he already has over CBS News. The FCC cap was only just repealed, so we’ve yet to see exactly how it will change the TV landscape. But don’t be surprised if you start to see a lot more broadcast mergers popping up in the news in this second half of the year.

Watch local channels with live TV streaming

The quickest and cheapest way to catch your local broadcast stations is with an OTA (over-the-air) antenna, but if you want to stream from anywhere on any device, a live TV streaming service is your best bet. Here’s some of our favorites:

YouTube TV

Best of the bestYouTube TV is the best live TV streaming provider on paper. For $82.99/mo., you get 100+ popular channels, including all of your local stations.

Hulu + Live TV

Editor’s ChoiceHulu + Live TV was our Editor’s Choice for the best live TV streaming provider in 2026. Our streaming experts are big fans of the service, which also gives customers access to its huge on-demand library with Hulu, Disney+, and ESPN Select (thanks, corporate mergers).

Still, I don’t often recommend streaming TV for seniors. A classic cable box is the way to go, keeping the TV experience familiar without throwing in a streaming service that, let’s face it, can require some frequent troubleshooting. DISH is a great TV service for rural folks, since its satellite service is available basically everywhere in the country as long as you’ve got a clear view of the sky to set up your antenna. Another reason why I like DISH so much is that it offers some senior discounts, unlike its rival DIRECTV. With DISH 55, customers aged 55 and older can get free in-home visits from DISH technicians, one free movie rental monthly, plus worry-free equipment protection. If you’re still not sure if DISH is the right fit to pair with CenturyLink internet, CenturyLink has a TV recommendation tool built into its website, which allows you to answer some questions about your TV habits in order to get a recommendation of the best TV provider for you.

item.title: Netflix Theft Leads to $105 Million Lawsuit Over Missing Nicolas Cage Movie Screener
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Netflix is in hot water this week as a new lawsuit aims to hold the streamer accountable for a stolen drive containing a Nicolas Cage film.
item.content:encoded:
An old-fashioned heist, but not for the Declaration of Independence

Simon Afram, a writer and producer from production company Op-Fortitude, filed a lawsuit against streaming giant Netflix last week. According to Afram, an associate producer brought an unreleased master copy of his upcoming film, a World War II film starring Nicolas Cage called “Fortitude,” to Netflix’s L.A. office in June. However, Netflix never returned the drive, as agreed upon. Instead, they reported that the movie was among a number of missing drives that had been stolen off a desk. Worried that this might impact the movie’s sales and distribution, Afram decided to sue Netflix for about $105,000,000. Netflix denies that it bears responsibility for the theft, but Afram disagrees. It’s a complicated issue, so let’s dive into the details.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

What is “Fortitude”?

”Fortitude” is an upcoming World War II film directed by Simon West. It boasts a star-studded cast, including Nicholas Cage, Ben Kingsley, Michael Sheen, and Ron Perlman. According to all the marketing, the movie is based on a real-life story about “the single most successful piece of orchestrated espionage in modern day history,” wherein British Intelligence operatives ran a series of scams to deceive the Nazis. Unfortunately, the only espionage the film ended up seeing was of the corporate kind.

How did this happen?

While “Fortitude” hasn’t yet resurfaced anywhere online, the whole thing makes me think of another scandal from earlier in the year: the Paramount leak that saw “Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender” spread across the internet months before its intended release. That leak happened because a hacker found his way into a media server, likely by acquiring an employee’s login credentials through another hack or phishing scheme. And the hacker bragged about his crimes online, so authorities were able to connect his online activity to his personally identifying information. But this breach is different. It was as simple as a drive swiped off a desk, and it’s much harder to trace. Netflix’s piracy division is reportedly “on high alert with the breach,” but still “disputes any claim that it bears the risk of loss for a film delivered without the proper industry-standard safeguards.” Basically, they’re keeping an eye out, but don’t want to pay the “Fortitude” team any money for the stolen content. They claim that Afram failed to properly protect the drive, but Afram says his team was only following Netflix’s instructions. He also claims that his associate producer told Netflix the drive was unencrypted, which should have been enough information to make Netflix store the drive in a more secure location. We don’t really know who had access to the office where Netflix kept the unencrypted “Fortitude” screener, or who took it. Was it a disgruntled employee? A rival producer? A team of kids speed-running the building like it’s a Scientology hub? It’s unclear, but we may get more clues if the stolen film reappears somewhere online. If you’d like to support the “Fortitude” team, avoid any leaks if/when they come out. If the movie gets a theatrical release, buy a ticket, or else legally watch it on whatever streaming service carries it on launch. I have a feeling it won’t be Netflix.

When it’s not fumbling confidential movie screeners, Netflix is a solid service full of fan-favorite shows like “Stranger Things” and “Bridgerton.”

item.title: Paramount Delays Merger With Warner Bros. — Here’s Why
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: After two major legal challenges, Paramount chose to pause the merger with Warner Bros. even longer. CableTV.com examines what this development means.
item.content:encoded:
Merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. could be delayed nearly a year

The temporary pause on the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery has been extended for quite some time. Paramount delayed merger proceedings on Friday, July 24, per court documents obtained by CableTV.com. The deal now won’t close until either five days after recent lawsuits are adjudicated or June 1, 2027 — whichever comes first. Legal experts told me last week that they were eying a crucial hearing early next month to see whether the proposed merger was truly in danger of falling apart. That hearing, per court documents, has now been canceled. Now, both sides are just waiting for the legal process to play out. “Last Friday’s agreement … is a significant win because the result is exactly what we have sought from the outset: a direct path to a trial based on the evidence,” Paramount said in a statement to CableTV.com. “This is the fastest and clearest way to prove that this transaction is good for competition, good for consumers, and good for creators, a conclusion dozens of competition authorities around the world have already reached. “Plaintiffs’ market definitions bear no relationship to the realities of today’s marketplace and cannot withstand scrutiny. We look forward to proving our case at trial.” Warner Bros. Discovery did not respond to a request for comment.

Paramount faced mounting legal pressure in recent weeks

The proposed Paramount-WBD merger, announced on February 27, had gained positive momentum in the past few months. In June, the U.S. Department of Justice approved the deal. Regulators in several other countries later followed suit, with the European Union being the latest to approve it. But the deal has recently faced legal challenges. First, attorneys general from 12 states sued to block the merger. Then the Writers Guild of America filed its own challenge. A handful of consumers even tried to block the merger, but their attempt was denied. Federal judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín, who was set to hear arguments on both lawsuits on August 3, initially granted a temporary restraining order of 14 days before extending it two more weeks. One day after that extension, Paramount chose to pause the deal.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

What comes next?

Paramount and the 12 states will prepare for trial, which will take months. The WGA also has a longer runway to get ready for the day it gets to make arguments in its own case against the merger. On August 4, Martínez-Olguín set the trial to start on March 2, 2027. The trial, she wrote in court documents, will last 12 days. Initially, the 12 states, WGA, and Paramount couldn’t reach an agreement on when the trial should start. The states and the WGA want it to begin on April 5, 2027. Paramount wants it to start on November 4, 2026. Meanwhile, everything involved with TV, film distribution, and streaming will stay status quo with Paramount and WBD. Consumers won’t have to worry about apps going away or news organizations skewing toward the Ellison family’s politics. And those who want the merger to succeed will be disappointed for the time being.

item.title: Your YouTube Premium Subscription Just Got a Lot More Valuable, Thanks to Peacock
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: YouTube Premium usually just removes ads from user-generated content, but beginning in 2027 it’ll also host Peacock shows and movies.
item.content:encoded:
YouTube adds Peacock content to its subscriptions

When Comcast decided to break up with NBCUniversal back in June, I speculated that Comcast would sell the entertainment company (and its streaming service, Peacock) to one of its competitors like Netflix or Amazon. But I never predicted what would actually end up happening. Instead of merging Peacock with Netflix or Prime Video, NBCUniversal turned to an unlikely business partner: Google. Google owns YouTube, and by extension, YouTube Premium, the service that removes ads from YouTube videos. (Note that YouTube Premium is different from YouTube TV, YouTube’s live TV streaming service. Hey, Google, maybe it’s time to start giving your sub-brands different names?) Thanks to this new deal with NBCUniversal, YouTube Premium subscribers will also be able to stream all Peacock content — like “PONIES,” “The Traitors,” and all the “Shrek” movies — directly on the platform. It’s sort of like bundling YouTube Premium with Peacock, except you’ll be able to watch everything in one place rather than juggling two apps. Want to know more? Read on for everything we know right now.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

What does this mean for current YouTube Premium subscribers?

YouTube Premium subscribers already got hit with a big change earlier this year when their plans suddenly got more expensive by two dollars a month. A typical YouTube Premium subscription now costs $15.99/mo., and this price hike didn’t come with any additional content. But beginning early in 2027, YouTube is going to start acquiring content from other streaming services. Everything you can get with a Peacock Premium subscription — which is normally $10.99/mo. and includes ads—will soon be available to stream directly on YouTube’s platform for YouTube Premium subscribers. Admittedly, it’s a little bit of a bait-and-switch. People who subscribe to YouTube Premium do so to avoid watching ads, and this new deal will put a bunch of ad-supported content back on their screens. It’s not yet clear whether subscribers can upgrade to Peacock Premium Plus, which removes ads. But assuming YouTube Premium’s price stays the same, and it only costs $15.99/mo. for the two services? That’s a pretty good value in this day and age. It’s an even better deal when you consider how many sports NBCUniversal has the rights to. According to the new press release, YouTube Premium subscribers will be able to watch “NFL, Olympics, NBA, MLB, Big Ten and Notre Dame Football, Big 12, Big East and Big Ten College Basketball, Premier League, WNBA, Kentucky Derby, golf” as part of this new bundle. What’s more, YouTube agreed to continue carrying NBCUniversal channels on its other service, YouTube TV, and NBC Sports will become YouTube’s main production partner for future live sports events.

With the addition of Peacock’s entire library, YouTube Premium is now more than just a really expensive ad blocker.
